value.title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs

facts.statement: Edge NPU performance depends on hardware capabilities, model transformation, and the overall deployment pipeline.
facts.limits: Abstract-level framing; not a measured result.
facts.quote: Edge NPU performance depends not only on hardware capabilities, but also on model transformation and the overall deployment pipeline.

facts.statement: The study proposes three configurations: Baseline, Vendor Guided NPU Only (VG-NPU), and Vendor Guided End-to-End (VG-E2E).
facts.limits: Methodology definition; not an empirical result.
facts.quote: We propose a benchmarking methodology that separates these effects by comparing three configurations: Baseline, Vendor Guided NPU Only (VG-NPU), and Vendor Guided End-to-End (VG-E2E)

facts.statement: VG-NPU preserves common model I/O and host-side processing; VG-E2E follows the vendor-native deployment pipeline.
facts.quote: where VG-NPU preserves common model I/O and host-side processing while VG-E2E follows the vendor-native deployment pipeline.

facts.statement: The methodology is applied to four edge NPUs and three vision workloads.
facts.quote: We apply this methodology to four edge NPUs and three vision workloads.

facts.statement: VG-NPU improves both accuracy and runtime-call latency in 10 of 12 NPU–workload combinations.
facts.limits: Measured under the study's configurations and workloads.
facts.quote: VG-NPU improves both accuracy and runtime-call latency in 10 of 12 NPU–workload combinations

facts.statement: VG-E2E reduces System-level latency in all combinations but improves accuracy in only four.
facts.limits: Measured under the study's configurations and workloads.
facts.quote: whereas VG-E2E reduces System-level latency in all combinations but improves accuracy in only four.

facts.statement: NPU-level performance rankings do not always match End-to-End rankings.
facts.quote: Moreover, NPU-level performance rankings do not always match End-to-End rankings

facts.statement: VG-E2E provides an additional 10.4–70.7% reduction in System-level latency over VG-NPU.
facts.limits: Reported range across combinations; not a single fixed value.
facts.quote: and VG-E2E provides an additional 10.4–70.7% reduction in System-level latency over VG-NPU.

facts.statement: The study defines three experimental conditions: Baseline, Vendor-Guided NPU-Only (VG-NPU), and Vendor-Guided End-to-End (VG-E2E).
facts.quote: we define three experimental conditions: Baseline, Vendor-Guided NPU-Only (VG-NPU), and Vendor-Guided End-to-End (VG-E2E).

facts.statement: Baseline permits only transformations required for NPU execution while limiting optional vendor-specific optimizations.
facts.quote: Baseline serves as a reference configuration that permits only the transformations required for NPU execution while limiting optional vendor-specific optimizations.

facts.statement: VG-NPU applies the vendor-guided model transformation recipe while preserving the same model inputs/outputs and host-side processing as Baseline.
facts.quote: VG-NPU applies the vendor-guided model transformation recipe while preserving the same model inputs and outputs and the same host-side processing as Baseline.

facts.statement: VG-E2E applies the full vendor-recommended deployment configuration, including native I/O formats, preprocessing, runtime execution, and postprocessing.
facts.quote: VG-E2E applies the full vendor-recommended deployment configuration, including native input/output formats, preprocessing, runtime execution, and postprocessing.

facts.statement: Under VG-NPU, both latency and accuracy improve in 10 of 12 NPU–workload combinations.
facts.limits: RQ1 result; specific to the evaluated NPUs/workloads.
facts.quote: First, under VG-NPU, both latency and accuracy improve in 10 of the 12 NPU–workload combinations.

facts.statement: Under VG-E2E, System-level latency decreases in all combinations, while accuracy decreases in eight.
facts.limits: RQ1 result; specific to the evaluated NPUs/workloads.
facts.quote: In contrast, under VG-E2E, System-level latency decreases in all combinations, while accuracy decreases in eight.

facts.statement: Vendor-guided optimization can improve both metrics at the controlled model-transformation level, but lower latency in final deployment does not necessarily imply preserved accuracy.
facts.quote: This result shows that vendor-guided optimization can improve both metrics at the controlled model-transformation level, but that lower latency in the final deployment does not necessarily imply preserved accuracy.

facts.statement: For YOLOv5m and YOLOv8s-pose, the relative NPU performance ranking remains unchanged; for ResNet50, it changes.
facts.limits: RQ2 result; based on three NPUs on the same host.
facts.quote: the relative performance ranking among NPUs remains unchanged for YOLOv5m and YOLOv8s-pose, but changes for ResNet50.

facts.statement: NPU-only performance does not reliably predict actual end-to-end performance; the relationship is workload-dependent.
facts.quote: This indicates that NPU-only performance does not, in general, reliably predict actual end-to-end performance, and that the relationship is workload-dependent.

facts.statement: VG-E2E achieves lower System-level latency than VG-NPU in all combinations, suggesting deployment-level processing can provide additional gains.
facts.limits: RQ3 result; gains cannot be attributed to a single optimization component.
facts.quote: Third, VG-E2E achieves lower System-level latency than VG-NPU in all combinations. This suggests that deployment-level processing can provide additional performance gains, while also indicating that such gains should not be attributed to any single optimization component.
